title: Geography Lec 1
summary: Latitudes are horizontal and longitudes are vertical imaginary lines; there are 181 latitudes and 360 longitudes in all.
The Equator (0°) is a great circle; Tropic of Cancer 23½° N, Tropic of Capricorn 23½° S, Arctic/Antarctic Circles 66½° N/S.

The Sun is overhead on the Tropic of Cancer on 21 June (summer solstice) and on the Tropic of Capricorn on 22 December (winter solstice); the equinoxes (Sun over the Equator) fall on 21 March and 23 September.
The Earth's axis is tilted at 23½°; beyond 66½° there are 6 months of day and 6 months of night. The Equator and both Tropics pass through Africa; the Equator does not pass through Europe.
8 states on the Tropic of Cancer: trick 'Gujarati Raja Made Chief Justice Win The Meeting' (Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, WB, Tripura, Mizoram).
15° = 1 hour, 1° = 4 minutes; IST is based on 82½° E (Mirzapur), 5½ hours ahead of GMT; the IDL follows 180° in the Pacific with zigzags.

India: latitude 8°4′–37°6′ N, longitude 68°7′–97°25′ E; N–S 3,214 km, E–W 2,933 km; westernmost Guhar Moti, easternmost Kibithu, northernmost Indira Col, southernmost Kanyakumari (Indira Point including islands).

Lakshadweep is the smallest UT (32.6 sq km); the 8° Channel separates Minicoy from the Maldives; Andaman and Nicobar are separated by the 10° Channel; Saddle Peak 732 m; Barren Island is an active volcano; capital Sri Vijaya Puram.
UNCLOS: internal waters, territorial sea 12 nautical miles, contiguous zone 24, EEZ 200, then the high seas; 1 nautical mile = 1.85 km.
India's land border is 15,106 km: Bangladesh > China > Pakistan > Nepal > Myanmar > Bhutan > Afghanistan; Bhutan states - 'BASA', Nepal - 'SUBU', Myanmar - 'Arunamami'.

Boundary lines: McMahon - China, Radcliffe - Pakistan/Bangladesh, Durand - Afghanistan/Pakistan; Sikkim: 35th (1974) and 36th (1975) Amendments, Article 371F; passes: Nathu La, Jelep La (Sikkim), Lipulekh, Mana, Niti (Uttarakhand).
Coastline about 11,098 km; 9 states and 4 UTs; Gujarat longest, Goa shortest; coasts: Malabar, Kannada, Konkan, Coromandel, Northern Circars, Utkal.
India has 6 physiographic divisions; the Thar is the world's most densely populated desert; the Chicken's Neck corridor and the Kaladan project (Sittwe port) are important.

Winds: trade winds, westerlies, polar easterlies; ITCZ/doldrums at the Equator, horse latitudes at 30°; Hadley, Ferrel and Polar cells; Coriolis force deflects right in the north, left in the south; southern westerlies: Roaring Forties, Furious Fifties, Shrieking Sixties.

Local winds: Loo, Chinook (snow eater), Bora and Mistral (cold), Sirocco, Harmattan (doctor wind), Khamsin; wind erosion forms yardangs, inselbergs, mushroom rocks, pediplains; deposition forms barchans, seifs, parabolic dunes.

mcqs.q: The tropical climatic zone is mainly confined to which latitudinal belt?
mcqs.e: The belt between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn is the Torrid Zone, where the Sun's rays fall vertically.

mcqs.q: Lines of latitude are imaginary lines of which type?
o: Lines that meet only at the poles
Lines that are all of equal length
mcqs.e: Latitudes are horizontal circles and longitudes are vertical lines; together they locate any place on a map.

mcqs.q: How many lines of latitude are there on the Earth in total?
mcqs.e: Equator (0°) + 90 north + 90 south = 181 latitudes.

mcqs.q: How many lines of longitude are there on the Earth in total?
mcqs.e: Longitudes run 0°–180° E and 0°–180° W, totalling 360.

mcqs.q: The Equator (0° latitude) forms the largest circle on the Earth and is therefore called a:
mcqs.e: The Equator divides the Earth into two equal hemispheres, northern and southern.

mcqs.q: The Tropic of Cancer lies at which latitude?
mcqs.e: 23½° N latitude is called the Tropic of Cancer.

mcqs.q: The Tropic of Capricorn lies at which latitude?
mcqs.e: The Sun's rays fall vertically only between the two Tropics.

mcqs.q: The Arctic Circle lies at which latitude?
mcqs.e: 66½° S is the Antarctic Circle; from these circles to the poles lies the Frigid Zone.

mcqs.q: The region between 23½° and 66½° latitude is called the:
mcqs.e: This zone receives slanting rays of the Sun, so temperatures are moderate.

mcqs.q: What happens when the Sun's rays fall slantingly?
o: There is no difference in heating
The rays spread over a larger area, so heating is less
The rays concentrate on a point and increase heating
mcqs.e: Direct rays concentrate on a smaller area and give more heat (like a convex lens).

mcqs.q: The shape of the Earth is known as:
mcqs.e: The Earth is slightly flattened at the poles, so it is not a perfect sphere.

mcqs.q: By how many degrees is the Earth's axis tilted?
mcqs.e: The axis is tilted 23½° from the vertical, i.e. it makes 66½° with the orbital plane.

mcqs.q: During the June solstice, which of these latitudes has the longest day (most daylight)?
mcqs.e: With the Northern Hemisphere tilted towards the Sun, areas beyond 66½° N get continuous daylight; the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer.

mcqs.q: On 21 June, the Sun's rays fall vertically on which line?
mcqs.e: This is the summer solstice: the longest day and shortest night in the Northern Hemisphere.

mcqs.q: On 22 December, the Sun's rays fall vertically on which line?
mcqs.e: This is the winter solstice: the longest night in the Northern Hemisphere.

mcqs.q: Which are the dates of the equinoxes, when day and night are equal?
mcqs.e: On these days the Sun is overhead at the Equator and day and night are equal everywhere.

mcqs.q: What is the event of 23 September called?
mcqs.e: The Vernal (Spring) Equinox falls on 21 March.

mcqs.q: Beyond which latitude (towards the poles) do six months of day and six months of night occur?
mcqs.e: Because of the Earth's tilt, polar day and night occur beyond the Arctic/Antarctic Circles.

mcqs.q: The Equator does NOT pass through which of the following continents?
mcqs.e: The Equator passes through Africa, South America and Asia (Indonesia, Maldives).

mcqs.q: Which continent is crossed by the Equator, the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn?
mcqs.e: Africa is also the continent with the largest number of countries.

mcqs.q: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which continent?
mcqs.e: The Tropic of Capricorn passes through South America, Africa and Australia.

mcqs.q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
mcqs.e: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

mcqs.q: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of these Indian states?
mcqs.e: Trick: 'Gujarati Raja Made Chief Justice Win The Meeting' (Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, WB, Tripura, Mizoram).

mcqs.q: The International Date Line (IDL) roughly follows which meridian?
mcqs.e: It runs through the Pacific and zigzags so that small island nations do not have two different dates.

mcqs.q: The International Date Line mainly passes through which ocean?
mcqs.e: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean.

mcqs.q: When crossing the International Date Line westwards (from America towards Asia), what must be done?
mcqs.e: Crossing eastwards, one day is subtracted.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct order of oceans from largest to smallest?
mcqs.e: The Arctic is the smallest ocean; the Indian Ocean is the only ocean named after a country.

mcqs.q: The Mariana Trench, the deepest point on Earth, lies in which ocean?
mcqs.e: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean.

mcqs.q: Which is the busiest ocean, shaped like the letter S?
mcqs.e: It lies between the Americas, Europe and Africa, making it the busiest trade route.

mcqs.q: In which ocean is the Sargasso Sea located, and what is it named after?
mcqs.e: It is a 'sea without shores', bounded only by ocean currents.

mcqs.q: What is the longitudinal extent of India?
mcqs.e: Memory trick: western limit 68° + about 30° gives 97–98°.

mcqs.q: What is the latitudinal extent of India?
mcqs.e: Adding about 29–30° to the southern limit of 8°4′ gives 37°.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate distance between two consecutive latitudes?
o: Least at the Equator and greatest at the poles
About 111 km, nearly the same everywhere
mcqs.e: In contrast, the distance between two longitudes is greatest at the Equator (111.32 km) and zero at the poles.

mcqs.q: Where is the distance between two longitudes the greatest?
mcqs.e: It decreases towards the poles and becomes zero at the poles.

mcqs.q: The 0° longitude (Prime Meridian) passes through which place?
mcqs.e: It is the basis of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT); it was chosen largely due to Britain's dominance.

mcqs.q: How many degrees does the Earth rotate in 1 hour, and how long does it take to rotate 1°?
mcqs.e: 360° ÷ 24 hours = 15° per hour, so 1° = 4 minutes.

mcqs.q: Into how many time zones is the Earth divided?
mcqs.e: Each time zone spans 15° of longitude.

mcqs.q: Indian Standard Time (IST) is based on which longitude?
mcqs.e: IST is 5½ hours ahead of GMT.

mcqs.q: By how much is IST ahead of GMT?
mcqs.e: 82.5° ÷ 15 = 5.5 hours; time is added when moving east.

mcqs.q: If it is 12 noon IST, what will be the approximate local time at 97½° E longitude?
mcqs.e: 97½° is 15° (1 hour) east of 82½°, so 1 hour is added.

mcqs.q: While calculating local time, what is done when moving east of Greenwich?
mcqs.e: Moving west, time is subtracted, because the Sun rises in the east.

mcqs.q: Which of the following cities is closest to the Prime Meridian (0°)?
mcqs.e: The westernmost place is nearest to 0°; Ahmedabad lies in western India.

mcqs.q: The 24° N latitude passes closest to the capital of which Indian state?
mcqs.e: Being just half a degree north of the Tropic of Cancer (23½°), it runs through central Madhya Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Which neighbouring country is separated from India by the Palk Strait?
mcqs.e: The Palk Strait lies between India and Sri Lanka, as does the Gulf of Mannar.

mcqs.q: Which two neighbouring countries share only a maritime (and no land) boundary with India?
mcqs.e: All the other listed neighbours share a land border with India.

mcqs.q: Which is the smallest island of Lakshadweep?
mcqs.e: Bitra has an area of only about 0.105 sq km.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest island of Lakshadweep?
mcqs.e: Andrott has an area of about 4.9 sq km.

mcqs.q: Which is the southernmost island of Lakshadweep?
mcqs.e: The Maldives begin just south of Minicoy.

mcqs.q: What separates Minicoy Island from the Maldives?
mcqs.e: The 8° Channel lies between Lakshadweep (Minicoy) and the Maldives.

mcqs.q: What is the capital of the Maldives?
mcqs.e: The language of the Maldives is Dhivehi; its President is Mohamed Muizzu.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate total area of Lakshadweep, which makes it India's smallest Union Territory?
mcqs.e: Lakshadweep is the smallest UT and Ladakh the largest.

mcqs.q: The Garo, Khasi, Jaintia and Naga hills join which north-south running hills?
mcqs.e: These are the Purvanchal hills; the Nilgiris are in the south and the Vindhyas-Satpuras in central India.

mcqs.q: Which neighbour of India is the only ASEAN member with which India shares a land border?
mcqs.e: Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan are not ASEAN members; Myanmar is India's gateway to ASEAN.

mcqs.q: When and where was ASEAN founded, and where is its headquarters?
mcqs.e: ASEAN stands for Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

mcqs.q: Which states are covered by the trick 'Arunamami' for Indian states bordering Myanmar?
mcqs.e: Myanmar was formerly Burma; its capital is Naypyidaw.

mcqs.q: Bhutan is known as the:
mcqs.e: Bhutan is known for its Gross National Happiness index and hydropower.

mcqs.q: What is a strait?
o: A group of islands in the sea
A strip of land joining two continents
A narrow waterway connecting/separating two large water bodies
mcqs.e: For example, the Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman.

mcqs.q: The Strait of Hormuz connects which two water bodies?
o: Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal
Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman
Andaman Sea and South China Sea
mcqs.e: It is a vital route for the global oil trade.

mcqs.q: Which Sri Lankan port has been leased to China for 99 years?
mcqs.e: It is a matter of strategic concern for India.

mcqs.q: Which Indian Union Territory claims a border with Afghanistan?
mcqs.e: Ladakh is also the largest Union Territory.

mcqs.q: Which Indian Union Territory is an island group in the Arabian Sea?
mcqs.e: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie in the Bay of Bengal.

mcqs.q: Which Union Territory has the highest sex ratio (1037)?
mcqs.e: This is as per Census 2011.

mcqs.q: The McMahon Line is the boundary between India and which country?
mcqs.e: The Radcliffe Line is between India and Pakistan/Bangladesh; the Durand Line between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

mcqs.q: The Radcliffe Line is the boundary between which countries?
mcqs.e: Drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe in 1947, when Bangladesh was East Pakistan.

mcqs.q: The Durand Line lies between which two countries?
mcqs.e: It is regarded as the international border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

mcqs.q: The 24th parallel, linked to the Sir Creek dispute, is related to which countries?
mcqs.e: Sir Creek lies between Gujarat (Kutch) and Sindh in Pakistan.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate east-west extent of the Indian mainland?
mcqs.e: Measured from Gujarat to Arunachal Pradesh; the north-south extent (Kashmir to Kanyakumari) is 3,214 km.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate north-south length of India?
mcqs.e: India's north-south extent is greater than its east-west extent.

mcqs.q: In which hemisphere does India lie?
mcqs.e: The Equator lies to India's south and the Prime Meridian to its west.

mcqs.q: The Standard Meridian of India (82½° E) passes through which five states?
o: Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Tamil Nadu
Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Telangana
Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Karnataka
mcqs.e: It passes through Mirzapur (UP), known for the Mirzapur Clock Tower reference, and Naini near Prayagraj.

mcqs.q: The IST meridian passes through which city, whose clock tower serves as its reference?
mcqs.e: 82½° E passes through Mirzapur (and Naini near Prayagraj).

mcqs.q: What is the approximate difference in local solar time between Gujarat (Guhar Moti) and Arunachal Pradesh (Kibithu)?
mcqs.e: About 30° of longitude = 2 hours; being in the east, the Sun rises earlier in Arunachal.

mcqs.q: Which is the easternmost village (inhabited point) of India?
mcqs.e: Guhar Moti (Gujarat) is India's westernmost inhabited village.

mcqs.q: Which is the westernmost inhabited village of India?
mcqs.e: Guhar Moti lies in the Kutch region.

mcqs.q: Which is the northernmost point of India?
mcqs.e: It lies in the Siachen region.

mcqs.q: Which is the southernmost point of the Indian mainland?
mcqs.e: Kanyakumari is also known as Cape Comorin.

mcqs.q: Which is India's southernmost point (including islands), submerged in the 2004 tsunami?
mcqs.e: Indira Point lies in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, not the mainland; it was submerged in the 2004 Boxing Day tsunami.

mcqs.q: Which country is called the 'Land of the Rising Sun'?
mcqs.e: In India, Arunachal Pradesh is called the 'Land of the Rising Sun'.

mcqs.q: Under UNCLOS, up to what distance from the baseline does India's territorial sea extend?
mcqs.e: 12 nautical miles is about 22 km.

mcqs.q: Into how many maritime zones does the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) divide the sea?
mcqs.e: Internal waters, territorial sea, contiguous zone, Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and high seas.

mcqs.q: Up to what distance from the baseline does the Contiguous Zone extend?
mcqs.e: Here a country can enforce customs, sanitary and similar laws.

mcqs.q: Up to what distance from the baseline does the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extend?
mcqs.e: The country has rights to explore and exploit resources here; beyond it lie the high seas (common heritage).

mcqs.q: 1 nautical mile is approximately equal to how many kilometres?
mcqs.e: It is the unit used to measure distances at sea.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the high seas is correct?
o: They are under India's control alone
They are part of the territorial sea
Only the coastal country may fish there
They are the common heritage of all nations; no country can claim them
mcqs.e: The high seas lie beyond the Exclusive Economic Zone (200 nautical miles).

mcqs.q: What is the updated (revised) total length of India's coastline?
mcqs.e: It was earlier taken as 7,516 km; the revised figure including islands is about 11,098 km.

mcqs.q: How many states and Union Territories in India have a coastline?
mcqs.e: The UT with the longest coastline is the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

mcqs.q: Which state has the longest coastline?
mcqs.e: As per the revised figures: Gujarat (about 2,340 km), Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh (trick 'GTA').

mcqs.q: Which state and which Union Territory, respectively, have the shortest coastlines?
mcqs.e: The UT with the longest coastline is the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a geographical feature bordering the Thar Desert?
mcqs.e: The Vindhyas lie in central India, far from the Thar.

mcqs.q: How many physiographic divisions does India have?
mcqs.e: Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Coastal Plains, Islands and the Thar Desert.

mcqs.q: Which is the most densely populated desert in the world?
mcqs.e: The Indian part of the Thar covers about 1.7–2 lakh sq km.

mcqs.q: Across which Indian states does the Thar Desert extend?
o: Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar
mcqs.e: The Thar is a hot desert lying west/north-west of the Aravallis.

mcqs.q: The India-Bhutan border is mainly defined by:
mcqs.e: The India-Bhutan and India-Nepal borders are open borders guarded by the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB).

mcqs.q: Which countries are covered by the trick 'Bachpan mein MBA' for India's land neighbours?
o: Bangladesh, China, Iran, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan, Afghanistan
Bangladesh, China, Pakistan, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan, Sri Lanka
Bangladesh, China, Pakistan, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan, Afghanistan
Bangladesh, China, Pakistan, Nepal, Maldives, Bhutan, Afghanistan
mcqs.e: India's total international land border is about 15,106 km; the countries are listed in decreasing order of border length.

mcqs.q: With which country does India share its longest land border?
mcqs.e: About 4,096 km; China 3,488, Pakistan 3,323, Nepal 1,751, Myanmar 1,643, Bhutan 699, Afghanistan 106 km.

mcqs.q: With which country does India share its shortest land border?
mcqs.e: The border with Afghanistan is about 106 km long.

mcqs.q: Which Indian state has the longest border with Bangladesh?
mcqs.e: States bordering Bangladesh: West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram.

mcqs.q: Which states are covered by the trick 'BASA' for states bordering Bhutan?
o: West Bengal, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Sikkim
West Bengal, Assam, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh
mcqs.e: The capital of Bhutan is Thimphu.

mcqs.q: Which states are covered by the trick 'SUBU' for states bordering Nepal?
o: Sikkim, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Assam, Uttarakhand
Arunachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Uttarakhand
Sikkim, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Uttarakhand
Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Uttarakhand
mcqs.e: Five Indian states border Nepal.

mcqs.q: As per the trick 'MAM Take Water', which is the correct list of states bordering Bangladesh?
o: Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Tripura, West Bengal
Meghalaya, Assam, Manipur, Tripura, West Bengal
Meghalaya, Assam, Mizoram, Nagaland, West Bengal
Meghalaya, Assam, Mizoram, Tripura, West Bengal
mcqs.e: Tripura is surrounded by Bangladesh on three sides.

mcqs.q: What is known as the 'Chicken's Neck' corridor?
o: Siliguri Corridor of West Bengal linking the North-East to the rest of India
mcqs.e: This narrow corridor lies between Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh and is strategically very sensitive.

mcqs.q: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Project connects India to which port of Myanmar?
mcqs.e: It runs from Kolkata via Sittwe to Mizoram, giving India alternative access to the North-East.

mcqs.q: Which Indian state is surrounded by Bangladesh on three sides?
mcqs.e: Tripura shares an international border only with Bangladesh.

mcqs.q: Which Indian state shares borders with China, Nepal and Bhutan?
mcqs.e: States bordering three countries: West Bengal (Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh), Sikkim (China, Nepal, Bhutan), Arunachal (China, Bhutan, Myanmar).

mcqs.q: West Bengal shares borders with which three countries?
mcqs.e: Its longest international border is with Bangladesh.

mcqs.q: Arunachal Pradesh shares borders with which three countries?
mcqs.e: Myanmar was formerly Burma; its capital is Naypyidaw.

mcqs.q: Which Constitutional Amendment gave Sikkim the status of an Associate State?
mcqs.e: The 36th Amendment (1975) made it a full state; Article 371F contains its special provisions.

mcqs.q: Which Article contains special provisions for Sikkim?
mcqs.e: Sikkim was earlier ruled by the Chogyal dynasty; it is India's least populous state.

mcqs.q: Which is the smallest state of India by population?
mcqs.e: Sikkim has the Nathu La and Jelep La passes.

mcqs.q: Which are the two major passes located in Sikkim?
mcqs.e: Both passes lie on the India-China (Tibet) border.

mcqs.q: In which state are the Lipulekh, Mana and Niti passes located?
mcqs.e: Muling La is another pass in Uttarakhand.

mcqs.q: The Lipulekh Pass lies at the tri-junction of which three countries?
mcqs.e: India and Nepal dispute Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura.

mcqs.q: The Kalapani dispute is between India and which country?
mcqs.e: Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura form a disputed area adjoining Uttarakhand.

mcqs.q: What is the name of the point where India, China and Myanmar meet?
mcqs.e: It marks the India-China-Myanmar tri-junction.

mcqs.q: Which of the following passes is NOT in Arunachal Pradesh?
mcqs.e: Nathu La is in Sikkim; Arunachal has Bum La, Bomdila, Yonggyap, Dihang and Diphu passes.

mcqs.q: In which part of India is the Coromandel Coast located?
mcqs.e: Eastern Coastal Plains: Utkal (Odisha), Northern Circars (Andhra), Coromandel (Tamil Nadu).

mcqs.q: What is the Kerala section of India's Western Coastal Plain called?
mcqs.e: The Karnataka section is the Kannada Coast and the Maharashtra-Goa section is the Konkan Coast.

mcqs.q: What is the coastal plain of Andhra Pradesh called?
mcqs.e: The coastal plain of Odisha is called the Utkal Coast.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly differentiates the Eastern and Western Coastal Plains?
o: The eastern coast is narrow and submerged
The eastern coast is wide and emergent; the western coast is narrow and submerged
The western coast is wide and emergent
mcqs.e: The wide eastern coast suits port development, but most of its ports are artificial.

mcqs.q: The Strait of Malacca connects which two water bodies?
o: Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea
Andaman Sea and South China Sea
Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman
mcqs.e: It is a major international trade route that gives the Andaman and Nicobar Islands strategic importance.

mcqs.q: What separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands?
mcqs.e: The Andamans lie north and the Nicobars south of the 10° Channel.

mcqs.q: The Duncan Passage separates which two islands?
mcqs.e: The 10° Channel separates Little Andaman from Car Nicobar.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
mcqs.e: Saddle Peak is in North Andaman; next come Mount Thuillier (Great Nicobar), Mount Diavolo (Middle Andaman) and Mount Koyob (South Andaman).

mcqs.q: Which is India's only active volcano, and where is it located?
mcqs.e: Narcondam is a dormant volcano; Barren Island lies in the Andaman Sea, east of the main Andaman group.

mcqs.q: What is the present name of Port Blair, the capital of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
mcqs.e: It is located in South Andaman; the islands cover about 8,249 sq km.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate total area of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
mcqs.e: Lakshadweep covers only about 32.6 sq km.

mcqs.q: Classification of winds: which are the three types of planetary (permanent) winds?
mcqs.e: Planetary winds blow across the globe; local winds blow only over limited areas.

mcqs.q: From which directions do the trade winds blow?
o: From the north-west in the Northern Hemisphere and south-west in the Southern
From the west in both hemispheres
From the north-east in the Northern Hemisphere and south-east in the Southern Hemisphere
Only from the east in both hemispheres
mcqs.e: A wind is named after the direction from which it blows.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly describes the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)?
o: It is the subtropical high-pressure belt
It is the westerly wind system
It is the equatorial low-pressure belt where the trade winds converge
It is a cold front zone
mcqs.e: The ITCZ is also called the doldrums (belt of calm).

mcqs.q: What are the doldrums?
o: The low-pressure belt around the Equator where the air is nearly calm
mcqs.e: Sailing ships got stranded here for lack of wind, hence the name.

mcqs.q: What is the belt located at about 30° N and 30° S called?
mcqs.e: Air subsides here, forming the subtropical high-pressure belt.

mcqs.q: Where is the subtropical high-pressure belt found?
o: At about 30° N and S (horse latitudes)
At the poles as a low-pressure zone
mcqs.e: Warm air rising at the Equator cools and descends here.

mcqs.q: Around which latitude is the sub-polar low-pressure belt found?
mcqs.e: The poles have high pressure (polar highs).

mcqs.q: Wind always blows in which direction?
o: From high pressure to low pressure
From low pressure to high pressure
Always from warm to cold areas
mcqs.e: Warm regions develop low pressure and cold regions develop high pressure.

mcqs.q: Which statement about warm and cold air is correct?
o: Warm air rises (low pressure) and cold air sinks (high pressure)
Warm air sinks and creates high pressure
Cold air rises and creates low pressure
mcqs.e: This is why a low-pressure belt forms at the Equator and a high-pressure belt at 30°.

mcqs.q: In the general circulation of the atmosphere, what is the cell between 0° and 30° called?
mcqs.e: The Ferrel cell lies between 30° and 60°, and the Polar cell from 60° to the pole.

mcqs.q: Which circulation cell forms between 30° and 60° latitude?
mcqs.e: The westerlies blow within the Ferrel cell.

mcqs.q: The Coriolis force arises because of:
mcqs.e: The resulting deflection of winds is described by Ferrel's law.

mcqs.q: Due to the Coriolis force, in which direction are winds deflected in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
o: Left in the north, right in the south
Right in the north, left in the south
mcqs.e: This produces the north-east and south-east trade winds.

mcqs.q: What names are given to the westerlies of the Southern Hemisphere?
o: Roaring Forties, Furious Fifties, Shrieking Sixties
mcqs.e: They blow very strongly at 40°, 50° and 60° S latitudes.

mcqs.q: Why are the westerlies so strong in the Southern Hemisphere?
o: Because there is little landmass to obstruct them
Because the Earth rotates faster there
mcqs.e: In the Northern Hemisphere, landmasses and structures create friction.

mcqs.q: What kind of wind is the Loo, and by what process is it produced?
o: A hot, dry local wind of North India; by horizontal transfer of heat (advection)
A cold local wind; by convection
A sea breeze; by pressure difference
A planetary wind; by the Coriolis force
mcqs.e: The Loo blows in summer, not all year; advection is the horizontal transfer of heat.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the Chinook is correct?
o: It is the 'doctor wind' of Africa
It is a warm wind of North America (Rockies), called the 'snow eater'
It is a dusty wind of the Sahara
It is a cold wind of Europe
mcqs.e: The Chinook melts snow rapidly, hence 'snow eater'.

mcqs.q: Bora and Mistral are what type of winds, and where do they blow?
mcqs.e: They are cold winds that blow mainly in winter.

mcqs.q: Which hot wind blowing from the Sahara towards the Mediterranean can cause 'blood rain'?
mcqs.e: Dust lifted from the desert gives the rain a reddish colour.

mcqs.q: Which wind is known as the 'Doctor Wind', and where does it blow?
mcqs.e: It is a dry wind considered beneficial to health.

mcqs.q: The Khamsin wind blows mainly in which country?
mcqs.e: It is a hot, dusty local wind of the Sahara region.

mcqs.q: What prevents cold winds from Central Asia/the Arctic from reaching North India?
mcqs.e: Without the Himalayas, North India would be extremely cold.

mcqs.q: What is the low-pressure belt near the Equator commonly called?
mcqs.e: It is where the trade winds converge and the air remains calm.

mcqs.q: What is the general direction of the jet stream that affects Indian climate in winter?
mcqs.e: The westerly jet stream brings winter rain (western disturbances) to north-west India.

mcqs.q: What is the significance of the westerly jet streams in winter?
o: They bring winter rainfall to North India
They cause the Loo in summer
mcqs.e: This rain benefits rabi crops such as wheat.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a depositional landform made by wind?
mcqs.e: Yardangs, inselbergs, mushroom rocks and pediplains are erosional landforms.

mcqs.q: Landforms are mainly shaped by which two processes?
mcqs.e: Wind, running water, glaciers and sea waves are the agents of these processes.

mcqs.q: Which is a correct group of landforms formed by wind erosion?
o: Barchan, seif, parabolic dune, transverse dune
mcqs.e: Wind-formed landforms are called aeolian landforms.

mcqs.q: What is characteristic of a 'seif' sand dune?
o: It forms in reverse direction due to vegetation
It forms perpendicular to the wind direction
It has two arms pointing in the wind direction
mcqs.e: A crescent dune with two arms is called a barchan.

mcqs.q: What is characteristic of a barchan dune?
o: Crescent-shaped, with two arms pointing downwind
A dune formed due to vegetation
Long dunes perpendicular to the wind
A sand dune with one arm
mcqs.e: It is a depositional sand landform.

mcqs.q: Where does a parabolic dune form, and which way do its arms point?
o: In open desert; arms point downwind
On river banks; arms follow the current
In vegetated areas; arms point upwind (against the wind)
In glacial areas; arms point downward
mcqs.e: Vegetation anchors the sand, so the arms trail behind.

mcqs.q: Moraines are formed by:
mcqs.e: A moraine is debris deposited by a glacier.

mcqs.q: What is the flat plain formed in deserts by erosion called?
mcqs.e: A peneplain results from river erosion, while a pediplain forms in arid regions by wind and sheet-wash erosion.

mcqs.q: What is a depression formed in deserts by wind erosion called?
mcqs.e: It is another erosional landform created by wind.
